items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Louis Baken came to my rescue... Baken would not accept one penny from me for the days I stayed in his flat.

ctx.x: I had not room reserved when I arrived in New York and I had not stayed in contact with my ex-girl friend Irene, whom I probably could have stayed with for a while. But Louis Baken came to my rescue. He had a 3 room apartment on 147th street, and told me that I could sleep in the front room on a folding couch until I found a room which I did after a few days. And Baken would not accept one penny from me for the days I stayed in his flat.

For some weeks I roomed with a woman named Mrs Fips on St.Nicholas Avenue. at the corner of 153rd street. Coleman Hawkins lived not far from me on 153rd street and also a bass player named John Brown. Whenever Illinois Jacquet came to New York, he stayed at this place and Mrs Fips always had a room reserved for him. Her son's name was Bobby and he knew many of the younger musicians and people in show business. It was Bobby who introduced me to Babs(Lee Brown) Gonzales.
